videos.script:
Every router link and every form control name in this course has been a directive: a class that works on an element already there. This lesson writes four of them.

{{attribute}} First a highlight, the classic. Its host bindings change the element it sits on, for the mouse and for the keyboard alike.

{{autofocus}} Then one the planner needs. When the add form opens, the focus should be in its first field, and the HTML attribute for that only works when the page loads. A directive does it every time.

{{structural}} A structural directive draws a template or does not. You write the opposite of n g if, and see what the star stands for.

{{control}} Then a directive that finds the form control on its own element, and sets aria invalid on every field, so no form has to write it again.

{{composition}} And host directives put a behaviour on a component from the inside.
